Sara (CS): Hey — Acme procurement just sent over a vendor scan asking for SOC2 scope details + DPA specifics. They specifically asked: do we store inference request payloads or user PII by default? Need a short, plain-English reply they can include in the questionnaire.

Nina (Security): Short answer: by default we do NOT persist request payloads. Metadata (latency, model id, token counts) are retained for 30 days for telemetry/ops. If a customer opts into request-logging for debugging, payloads are stored encrypted and access-controlled. Happy to draft. :+1:

Ben (Eng): Adding detail: hosted API flow — request hits edge -> routed to runtime -> we stream tokens and write ephemeral traces. Only when "request_logging: true" in account config do we write full payloads to S3-like storage, encrypted with customer KMS if configured. KV cache never persisted across sessions.

Liam (PM): Nice. @Nina can you make a ~3 sentence blurb + a 1-line SOC2 mapping (control IDs) so procurement can check boxes? They also asked if we have subprocessors for logs.

Nina (Security): Draft incoming: "Redwood does not retain customer request payloads unless explicitly enabled by the customer. Operational telemetry (latency, model identifier, token counts) is retained for 30 days to support performance and reliability. When request logging is enabled, logs are stored encrypted and subject to role-based access; customers may configure KMS key usage and retention policies via the Console."

Nina (Security): SOC2 mapping: CC6.1 (access controls), CC7.1 (system configuration), CC8.2 (data retention) — we cover these via RBAC, KMS, and retention policies. (this is a simplified pointer for procurement, not a formal attestation)

Sara (CS): Perfect. Procurement also wants to know whether we share telemetry with third-party analytics vendors.

Ben (Eng): We send aggregated telemetry to our monitoring provider (metrics only, no request payloads or PII). Exception: if a customer enables a third-party integration, that is opt-in.

Aisha (Legal): Looping in — I can sign off on the blurb and add the DPA clause references. @Sara do we have the specific clause numbers they want? If not, I'll attach the DPA excerpt.

Sara (CS): Not yet. They gave a generic form with checkboxes. Could you attach the DPA excerpt we typically share for hosted customers?

Aisha (Legal): Will do. I'll attach DPA_excerpt_v3 and a short note on data residency/transfer. Expect in ~2 hours.

onboard-bot: Document uploaded: https://redwood.docs/internal/acme/dpa_excerpt_v3.pdf

Liam (PM): Thanks — action items: Nina finalizes 3-sentence blurb, Aisha attaches DPA excerpt and clause refs, Sara to send consolidated reply to Acme procurement. Target: EOD tomorrow.

Sara (CS): Assigned. I'll ping if they ask for SOC2 report extract (we can provide the attestation pdf). :eyes:

Ben (Eng): If they request logs examples for integration, we should provide sanitized snippets only.

Nina (Security): I'll add one sanitized sample line they can include for clarity.

Sara (CS): Great — closing thread for now, will reopen if procurement follows up. Thanks all :clap:
